messages.content: Generate a synthetic C# .NET 8 performance dataset record. Return only a JSON object with exactly three string fields: baseline_code, candidate_code, time_label. Each code field must be a complete public static class Candidate containing the requested public static Run method, with fully qualified library type names. Both implementations must satisfy the contract without modifying inputs. time_label describes candidate runtime relative to baseline for the stated workload: faster, slower, or uncertain. The candidate is an alternative, not necessarily faster. Do not include benchmarks, comments claiming measured results, or text outside JSON.

Signature: public static long Run(int[] values, int threshold)
Contract: Return the long sum of values satisfying (value >= threshold), using signed int comparisons. The array is non-null; do not mutate it. Sum in long. Empty arrays or no selected values return zero.
Baseline implementation: Allocate System.Collections.Generic.List<int>(values.Length). Store indices satisfying (value >= threshold). Call ToArray exactly once after the scan, then iterate that index array to sum selected values in a long accumulator. No early no-match return. Do not substitute List traversal for ToArray.
Candidate implementation: Scan values once and sum values satisfying (value >= threshold) directly into a long accumulator. No collections, arrays or LINQ; no unsigned casts.
Workload: The array has 64 elements and none satisfies the specified selection predicate.
Array setup is outside the measured method; all construction inside Run is included. Use a 5% relative threshold when describing a speed difference; use uncertain if unable to decide.

Signature: public static long Run(int[] left, int[] right)

Candidate implementation: Construct one System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<int> from right. Visit every left position, query Contains, then add (long)i+1 when found. Do not deduplicate left. No LINQ.
Workload: Both arrays have 64 elements; every left value equals right[0]; right has distinct values.
Array setup is outside the measured method; all construction inside Run is included. Use a 5% relative threshold when describing a speed difference; use uncertain if unable to decide.
